subject: paediatrics
title: Persistent Diarrhoea, Dysentery, Cholera and Hypokalaemia

steps.tx: Protracted diarrhoeal episodes continuing beyond two weeks carry catastrophic risks of severe acute malnutrition. By definition, **pediatric persistent diarrhoea** represents an episode of presumed infectious etiology starting acutely and lasting fourteen days or longer. Persistent mucosal blunting, secondary disaccharidase deficiency, and bacterial overgrowth disrupt enterocyte absorption, accounting for over thirty-five percent of all diarrhoeal child deaths.
steps.say: Persistent diarrhoea starts acutely and lasts fourteen days or longer. It damages the intestinal lining and impairs nutrient absorption, causing over a third of diarrhoeal deaths.

vis.caption: Persistent diarrhoeal nutritional decline, secondary disaccharidase loss, and therapeutic dietary algorithms. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Invasive colonic mucosal ulceration causes painful bloody stools accompanied by systemic toxicity. The syndrome termed **bacillary dysentery** presents with acute passage of loose stools containing visible blood and mucus, accompanied by high fever, severe abdominal cramps, and painful tenesmus. It is caused primarily by Shigella flexneri and Shigella dysenteriae type 1, which invade enterocytes and elaborate cytotoxic Shiga toxins, producing mucosal necrosis.
steps.say: Bacillary dysentery features acute bloody, mucoid stools with fever and tenesmus, caused by invasive Shigella. It causes mucosal necrosis and risks haemolytic uraemic syndrome.

left.title: Bacillary Dysentery (Shigellosis)
points: Acute onset with high fever and severe cramps
Frequent scant stools with frank blood and mucus
Caused by invasive Shigella, Campylobacter, or Salmonella
High risk of toxic megacolon and rectal prolapse

right.title: Amoebic Dysentery (Entamoeba)
points: Insidious onset with mild or absent fever
Bulky foul-smelling stools mixed with dark blood
Caused by Entamoeba histolytica trophozoites
Flask-shaped colonic ulcers; treat with metronidazole

steps.tx: Empirical antimicrobial therapy must eradicate invasive Shigella to prevent life-threatening complications. Children presenting with bloody diarrhoea require immediate **ciprofloxacin for dysentery** (15 mg/kg twice daily for three days) as the first-line oral antimicrobial. Ciprofloxacin rapidly clears bacterial excretion, halts mucosal necrosis, and prevents systemic complications such as toxic encephalopathy, leukaemoid reactions, and Shiga toxin-mediated haemolytic uraemic syndrome.
steps.say: Treat dysentery immediately with oral ciprofloxacin at fifteen milligrams per kilogram twice daily for three days. This eradicates Shigella and prevents haemolytic uraemic syndrome.

rows: 10 mg/kg three times daily for 7 days
Used only when amoebic trophozoites confirmed

steps.tx: Secretory enterotoxin-mediated hypersecretion precipitates fulminant dehydration within hours of onset. Infection with Vibrio cholerae produces classic **cholera rice-water diarrhoea**, characterized by sudden, profuse, painless watery stools with a fishy odour containing flecks of mucus and epithelial debris. Vibrio cholerae enterotoxin irreversibly ADP-ribosylates G-alpha-s proteins, constitutively activating adenylate cyclase to drive massive, uncontrolled chloride and water secretion.
steps.say: Cholera causes sudden profuse rice-water diarrhoea driven by cholera enterotoxin activating adenylate cyclase. Fluid loss can exceed one litre per hour, demanding emergency IV rehydration.

left.title: Cholera Toxin Secretory Mechanism
points: B subunit binds enterocyte GM1 ganglioside receptor
A subunit ADP-ribosylates stimulatory G-protein
Persistent cAMP elevation opens CFTR chloride channels
Massive secretory water loss exceeding 1 L/hour

right.title: Emergency Cholera Management
points: Immediate IV Ringer's lactate via Plan C protocol
Replaces massive stool losses volume-for-volume
Single-dose oral azithromycin (20 mg/kg) or doxycycline
Shortens excretion and decreases total volume by 50%

steps.tx: Viral enterotoxin synthesis and villous tip destruction drive severe winter infantile gastroenteritis. The most prevalent cause of severe dehydrating diarrhoea in infants under two years is **rotavirus gastroenteritis**, transmitted via feco-oral spread. Viral non-structural protein 4 (NSP4) acts as a viral enterotoxin, mobilizing intracellular calcium to stimulate chloride secretion, while viral replication destroys mature absorptive enterocytes, provoking severe osmotic and secretory diarrhoea.
steps.say: Rotavirus causes severe dehydrating diarrhoea in young infants through enterocyte blunting and NSP4 enterotoxin. Live oral rotavirus vaccines at six, ten, and fourteen weeks prevent disease.

vis.caption: Bedside evaluation of dehydration severity, sunken eyes, and abdominal skin pinch in viral gastroenteritis. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Massive gastrointestinal potassium excretion depletes total-body intracellular electrolyte reserves. Severe watery diarrhoea frequently precipitates **hypokalaemia in diarrhoea**, characterized by serum potassium concentrations falling below 3.5 milliequivalents per litre. Clinical manifestations include generalized muscular hypotonia, weakness, diminished deep tendon reflexes, abdominal distension secondary to paralytic ileus, and dangerous cardiac arrhythmias with flattened T waves and prominent U waves.
steps.say: Diarrhoea causes severe potassium loss, leading to muscle weakness, paralytic ileus, and cardiac arrhythmias with U waves on ECG. Standard ORS replaces potassium safely.

rows: Flattening of T waves on ECG
ST segment depression, U waves appear
Prolonged PR, prominent U waves, ventricular VT
Potassium shifts into cells with bicarbonate

steps.tx: Secondary loss of brush border lactase enzyme provokes severe osmotic fermentation. Persistent injury to villous tips causes **secondary disaccharidase lactose intolerance**, where unabsorbed dietary lactose in milk feeds ferments in the colon, producing lactic acid and hydrogen gas. The infant passes explosive, frothy, acidic stools with a pH below 5.5, triggering severe perineal excoriation and positive stool reducing substances.
steps.say: Damage to brush border enzymes causes secondary lactose intolerance. Unabsorbed lactose ferments into acid, producing explosive frothy stools that excoriate the buttocks.

left.title: Lactose Intolerance Signs
points: Explosive watery stools following milk feeds
Stool pH <5.5 (acidic due to lactic acid)
Stool reducing substances >0.5% (Benedict test)
Severe perianal erythema and raw skin breakdown

right.title: Dietary Management Protocol
points: Continue breastfeeding unhindered (protective factors)
Replace animal milk with yoghurt or low-lactose diet
Or temporary lactose-free formula for 2 to 3 weeks
Spontaneous recovery as enterocytes regenerate

steps.tx: Evidence-based dietary algorithms restore enterocyte regeneration in persistent childhood diarrhoea. Under IMNCI and WHO guidelines, children with persistent diarrhoea without severe dehydration are managed using the **initial persistent diarrhoea diet** (Diet A), which replaces animal milk with reduced-lactose feeds like curd or yoghurt, combined with energy-dense cereals (rice, lentils, vegetable oil) and continuous breastfeeding. If diarrhoea persists at seven days, a non-lactose egg-based diet (Diet B) is introduced.
steps.say: Manage persistent diarrhoea using yoghurt-based reduced-lactose diets with rice and oil. If diarrhoea persists after one week, switch to a lactose-free egg and glucose diet.

rows: Start on Day 1 for 7 days; continue breast milk
Cooked egg white, puffed rice, glucose, oil
If Diet A fails at 7 days; feed for 7 days
Elemental amino acid or semielemental formula
Double RDA of multivitamins & zinc (20 mg)
